execution_head_note: The later HEAD registers Work progress only; the AU/AT/AR runtime and saved comparison inputs are unchanged.

reconstruction.selection: All four AU natural returns with unlearned bases, at least 400 unspent units and a fresh unpurchased offer before that return's purchase and surplus conversion. Prefixes are reconstructed once each and checked against AU. No synthetic funds, altered offer or respec to afford a purchase.
reconstruction.checkpoint_boundary: After return settlement and offer generation, before purchase and current-return surplus conversion. Earlier prefix returns retain AU's original sale/preparation policy. Neither comparison branch converts surplus at this boundary.

comparison.preparation: AR adapt for C and AU use_owned deck, including their existing deterministic tie breaks.
comparison.learning_first: Run existing AR preparation first, then consider a candidate using only remaining unspent funds; after an actual purchase, prepare again.
comparison.acquisition_first: Consider one candidate using the checkpoint's actual 400 unspent units; then run exactly the same AR preparation and AU deck selection. No learning refund is performed to finance the purchase.
comparison.candidate_order: Evaluate each affordable candidate only on a copy: purchase, AR C adapt, AU use_owned deck. Keep candidates actually selected into the resulting legal deck or equipment. Order cards first as in AU; passive candidates then use the existing C home_value plus affix_value divided by equipment cost; finally candidate ID. Card and passive scores are never directly compared. Skip if no candidate is selected. Do not inspect combat draws, actions or outcomes.
comparison.seed: Use each checkpoint's native next seed: 2, 3, 10, 11. Both policies share it within each pair. The four histories also share portions of earlier seed sequences, so they are not independent human win-rate samples.

record: Checkpoint unspent units, actual paid learning fees, fully refundable learning amount, available candidates and owned copies
Purchase affordable, learned-base equipment eligibility, legal preparation selection, reason for skipping each candidate
Actual before-purchase funds, purchase spending, paid learning fee allocation before/after, preparation differences, remaining units
Bought card or passive selected at departure, player use before/after refill, NPC use and field material use, exact passive-instance trigger counts
Clear/defeat, player actions, time, remaining HP, receipts, preserved old ownership and unchanged checkpoint
AU prefix preparation/receipt/boundary equality, purchase replay, first-action save restoration and input hashes
limits: Only one diagnostic next C expedition per branch, not the original automatic A/B route after clearing C.
All four checkpoints have already cleared C. This does not show that early purchases help the first C clear.
A purchase that requires explicitly refunding learned bases is a separate choice and is excluded.
Current-return surplus conversion is deferred in both branches; no claim about strategies funding purchases by sale.
No exhaustive candidate/deck optimization, new combat seeds, price changes, formal numerical adoption, UI implementation or human enjoyment claim.
Basic design 0.53 and D53 remain unchanged.
